name: web-ai-showcase site-wide audio provenance ledger
description: Every audio file bundled with the site, keyed by content hash, with a fail-closed licensing contract. Mirrors image-provenance/ledger.json: an audio file ships only if its bytes map to an entry here — either reconciled (licence + source + attribution) or explicitly declared legacy-unreconciled against a frozen baseline. media/manifest.json audioAssets[] remains the media-LIBRARY record for non-image media-library samples; this ledger is the site-wide record for every bundled audio file.
policy: Every tracked audio file (.wav .mp3 .ogg .m4a .flac) MUST have an entry keyed by its content hash. A new, changed, or copied audio file whose bytes are not in this ledger FAILS the gate — record provenance first, do not ship first and document later.
A reconciled entry (rightsCleared: true) MUST carry provenance.kind (licensed | first-party), a license, a traceable source (sourceUrl or sourceAsset), and a non-empty attribution string.

Audio bundled BEFORE this gate existed has no rights record. It is declared, one content hash at a time, as archetype 'legacy-unreconciled' with an explicit legacyReason, and its hash is frozen in legacyBaseline.hashes. The legacy set can only shrink: declaring a NEW asset legacy FAILS the gate.

This ledger neither resolves nor ratifies the TED clip rights question (bead web-ai-showcase-z79) — it records the ted.wav bytes as legacy/unreconciled so the decision stays with the owner while every copy becomes visible.
A path may belong to exactly one content hash, and every ledger path must be a tracked file (no orphan rows).

legacyBaseline.note: origin/main at the commit that introduced this gate. Every entry below is out of scope (never retroactively passed), exactly like check-portfolio-acceptance.mjs's 294 legacy families: it shipped with no rights record and this gate does not invent one. The frozen set is explicit content hashes, not a filename pattern — the ted.wav bytes (11 copies, hash 0013db1382f6…) and the jfk.wav bytes (17 copies, hash 627f0e49f927…) are named so the TED rights decision (bead z79) is not pre-empted, and any asset added after this baseline must be reconciled.

entries.legacyReason: JFK 1961 inaugural address excerpt (US federal work, public domain) — but every copy ships under a different sample name (sample-speech, sample-sentence, sample-eng, speech, …) and only one path was ever recorded in media/manifest.json. Declared unreconciled as a group; a per-copy reconcile promotes it to archetype 'licensed'.
